title: Singapore's Broadcast Rights for 2020 Tokyo Olympics
what_it_is: Singapore's Broadcast Rights for 2020 Tokyo Olympics

sections.label: Olympics broadcast rights negotiations
sections.summary: The passage states negotiations over broadcast rights are best left to broadcasters and rights owners, citing rising costs and cheaper viewing options.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The negotiations are best left to the broadcasters and rights owners to undertake and conclude, as it would be unwise to take the position that we should have "live" telecasts regardless of the cost and for the Government to underwrite any amount demanded by rights owners, particularly when the rights are still being negotiated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: For instance, for the 2016 Rio Olympics broadcasting rights, Dentsu originally wanted to charge three times what it cost to broadcast the 2012 London Olympics "live".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: At the same time, it is becoming increasingly difficult for broadcasters to recoup the escalating costs of broadcasting rights, because there are so many cheaper options to watch such sporting events "live".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
sentences.text: If the rights owners only seek to maximise their profits, they risk making broadcasts of major games less accessible by driving fans to other media channels or away from the sports entirely.

sections.label: Pooling resources for broadcast rights
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the broadcaster and Government would pool resources for rights, and states it is best not to intervene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: In light of the last Olympics when we had Joseph Schooling doing Singapore proud in 30 seconds, would the broadcaster consider together working with the Government to think about pooling resources to secure the rights?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: As the Minister rightly said, the cost of securing the rights has gone up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
sentences.text: This has been done in Malaysia and in other countries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: It is best that we leave it to the rights owners and the broadcasters to make the negotiations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
sentences.text: The most important thing is that we do not think it is right for us to intervene.
